# MINIMAX H3 — ONE REUSABLE DIGITAL-HUMAN PROMPT

Write one production-ready English REF2VA prompt for the entire long-form presenter video. The same prompt is reused for every automatically scheduled Clip.

REFERENCE ROLES
- <Picture 1>: facial identity, facial structure, hairstyle and age.
- <Picture 2>: wardrobe, body proportions, posture and environment.
- <Audio 1>: authoritative narration timing, phonemes, mouth/jaw motion, breathing and expression timing.

CONTINUITY RULES
- Preserve the same identity, wardrobe, accessories, framing, lighting, camera and environment for the full timeline.
- Clip 1 establishes the shot. Later Clips inherit a protected verified latent tail and must continue its exact pose, gesture, expression and camera state.
- Do not reset the scene, change clothing, reframe, zoom, add speech, paraphrase narration or invent audio.
- Use restrained, context-aware presenter gestures and keep the mouth readable.
- Describe persistent attributes, not Clip-specific events or timestamps, because this one prompt drives all Clips.

Use clear REF2VA sections: subject_definitions, program_style, summary, retention_analysis, detailed_description, overall_soundscape and non_diegetic_audio. Return exactly one complete prompt.

WF Guide

1. Select the master audio and reference images.
2. Write one prompt in the reusable MiniMax H3 Reference to Video node.
3. Keep Timeline Mode at Auto from Audio. Manual is only for deliberate overrides.
4. Click Run/resume checkpoints → assemble on DIGITAL HUMAN PROJECT.

The planner measures decoded audio, computes the required Clip count, and queues this same generation pipeline once per Clip. Every Clip remains an independent checkpoint job; models are released between jobs. Do not queue the full graph.

nodes.title: Reusable Clip — MiniMax H3 Reference to Video
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is the same professional presenter defined jointly by <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>.

<Picture 1> has priority for facial identity, facial structure, hairstyle, age appearance, skin appearance, and personal identity.

<Picture 2> has priority for full-body appearance, wardrobe, body proportions, presenter posture, and professional studio environment.

<Audio 1> is the protected narration audio track for this clip.

<Audio 1> is the only source of speech timing.

<Audio 1> controls:
- phoneme timing
- lip synchronization
- mouth movement
- jaw movement
- facial expression timing
- breathing rhythm

The same <Subject 1> identity must be preserved throughout all clips.

Do not change:
- facial identity
- gender appearance
- age appearance
- hairstyle
- clothing
- accessories
- body proportions
- studio environment


program_style:

This is a professional informational presenter program.

The visual style is:

- professional broadcast news style
- realistic human presentation
- trustworthy
- authoritative
- clear
- friendly

The presenter behaves like a professional studio presenter explaining the supplied narration.

Avoid:
- advertising style
- cinematic style
- exaggerated performance
- dramatic expressions


summary:

[reference generation]

Generate a professional informational presenter video.

<Subject 1> presents the protected narration clearly and naturally.

The presenter maintains a calm, professional, and approachable broadcast presentation style.

The video should look like a high-quality studio information program.


retention_analysis:

<Subject 1>:

fully_preserved -

Preserve the exact presenter identity defined by <Picture 1> and <Picture 2>.

Maintain:

- identical face
- identical hairstyle
- identical clothing
- identical body proportions
- identical studio environment
- identical lighting style

Only allow:

- natural mouth movement
- natural blinking
- subtle facial expression changes
- context-aware presenter gestures


Camera:

fully_preserved -

Preserve:

- camera position
- camera height
- focal length
- perspective
- framing
- composition

The camera setup remains identical throughout the clip.

No:

- camera drift
- reframing
- zoom
- push in
- pull out
- pan
- tilt


<Audio 1>:

fully_preserved -

The spoken audio must be followed exactly.

Do not:

- add extra words
- remove words
- modify spoken content
- generate additional speech


detailed_description:

The target video is a realistic professional informational presenter program.

The video uses a vertical 9:16 locked-off broadcast composition.

[Shot 1]

A static medium shot captured by a fixed tripod camera.

The camera position, camera height, focal length, perspective, and framing remain unchanged throughout the entire clip.

The camera does not move.

No zoom.
No push in.
No pull out.
No pan.
No tilt.
No reframing.

<Subject 1> appears in the professional studio environment defined by <Picture 2>.

The presenter remains at the same distance from the camera throughout the entire shot.

The presenter maintains the exact composition defined by the reference image.

The lighting remains consistent with <Picture 2>.

The presenter maintains direct eye contact with the camera.

The presenter has a calm, friendly, and trustworthy expression.

The presenter maintains a professional broadcast posture.


The presenter uses natural, context-aware hand gestures that match the spoken content.

The gestures follow the meaning and rhythm of the narration naturally, similar to a professional television presenter.

The gestures should emphasize important policy points when appropriate.

Hand movements are subtle, controlled, and professional.

Avoid exaggerated arm movements or dramatic gestures.

The presenter remains within the original camera framing.


The presenter speaks naturally.

The mouth movement, jaw movement, and facial expression timing must accurately follow the phoneme sequence of <Audio 1>.

The presenter does not add any extra speech or sound.

Do not summarize, paraphrase, or modify the spoken content.


For continuation clips:

Continue the exact previous frame state.

The first frame must seamlessly continue from the previous clip ending.

Preserve:

- same facial position
- same body position
- same camera framing
- same camera perspective
- same clothing
- same lighting
- same studio environment

The camera remains locked in the same static shot.

The presenter continues the natural speaking motion and context-aware gestures from the previous clip.

No visual reset.

No scene transition.


overall_soundscape:

<Audio 1> is the protected narration audio.

The narration is clear and isolated.

No additional voice.

No environmental speech.


non_diegetic_audio:

No background music.

<Audio 1> is the only audio source.

<Audio 1> drives:

- lip synchronization
- mouth movement
- facial expression timing
- speaking rhythm
